messages:
ara: Heads-up — after swapping to the new INT8 kernel for Mistral-7B we saw a ~12% throughput drop for short-chat workloads. wondering if anyone has calibration artifacts or batching heuristics to blame :thinking_face:

samir: I repro'd locally. FP8 kernels still fastest for 512 tokens, INT8 slower on our A100 kernel path. p99 latency +30ms on small batches (batch_size<=4). I have pprof traces.

jess: did you also switch the microbatching policy? small batches + continuous batching changes can amplify kernel startup cost. try enabling dynamic_microbatch: true and lower target_batch_ms to 8ms.

samir: good call — toggling dynamic microbatching recovers ~6% of throughput. but p99 still worse than before. the profiler points at KV cache memcpy during decode: big memmove calls right before kernel dispatch.

maria: yeah saw that too. trace shows heavy host->device tile copy when using the INT8 kernel because we changed the weight layout to blocked-4. memcpy pattern changed from a big contiguous copy to many small tiled memcpys. that kills throughput for tiny sequences.

ara: any quick mitigation? change kernel? reorder copy?

maria: two options: 1) change fallback kernel to one that accepts the blocked layout (avoids extra reformat), 2) batch the KV-copy operations into single batched cudaMemcpyAsync calls. I wrote a small patch to coalesce tile copies — reduces memcpy overhead by ~45% in my local run.

samir: posting perf summary from my runs:
```
model  | kernel | batch | tpks/s | p99(ms) | notes
M7B    | FP8    | 1     |  98    |  210    | baseline
M7B    | INT8   | 1     |  86    |  240    | new int8 kernel w/ tiled copies
M7B    | INT8   | 1+dmb |  92    |  228    | dynamic_microbatch enabled
L70B   | 4-bit  | 2     |  12    |  850    | quantized 4-bit, slow kernel for MLPs
Q7B    | INT8   | 4     | 180    |  120    | good speed on our int8-qkern
```

jess: thanks. could you also share the calib config you used? i want to check per-channel vs per-tensor scales and layernorm handling.

samir: sure — here is the calib command i ran in the infra repo:
```
quant-calib --model mistral-7b --mode per-channel --steps 2048 --dataset /mnt/calib/dialog_short.jsonl --bias-correction true --save-profile /tmp/m7b_int8_profile.json
```

samir: important note: enabling bias-correction improved downstream perplexity but increased kernel latency slightly (more quant ops). for Mistral we saw a small quality boost; for Llama-70B bias-correction had negligible benefit and cost was not worth it.

maria: additional probe: when we run the same INT8 kernel but keep weights in row-major (no blocked transform) and only do blocked transform on first load (amortized), KV memcpy pattern is friendlier. might be a codegen change in kernel that assumes blocked layout. i'll open a PR to either accept row-major or perform a single pretransform for serving path.

ara: can we store per-model recommended profile + serving hints in the repo? e.g., "mistral-7b": {prefer: FP8, int8_profile: X, batch_hint: small_chat}. we should push those to the model catalog so dedicated/dedicated-private can auto-apply.

jess: yes please. model-level metadata fields we want: quant_recommendation, fallback_kernel, microbatching_hint, kv_copy_strategy. sample schema i propose:
```
{
  "quant_recommendation": "FP8",
  "fallback_kernel": "int8-blocked4-v2",
  "microbatching_hint": "enable_dynamic",
  "kv_copy_strategy": "coalesce-tiles"
}
```

perf-bot: benchmark run completed for branch mixed-quant-kernel-fix — M7B INT8 throughput delta: +9% after coalesce-tiles patch. details: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/1851234500 :tada:

samir: nice. next action items: maria to PR kernel pretransform/coalesce-tiles (blocking memcpy), jess to add model metadata entries for Mistral/Qwen/Llama, i'll run full eval (SQuAD/LLM-ops prompt-suite) to check repro quality regressions. i'll also add a small unit test that asserts memcpy count < 8 for decode path.

maria: on it, i'll push a draft tonight.

jess: i'll add model catalog entries and a rollout plan (canary on Hosted first).

ara: great. thanks everyone. keeping notes here for postmortem. :memo:
